the three crops show the loose end of the roll lying on a green cloth, the paper crumpled and creased. Crop 3 carries eight or nine characters of very faint pencil cursive along the extreme edge of the paper, running the length of the roll; the strokes are letters rather than figures and no word or date could be made out at this resolution, under median filtering, high-pass filtering and paper-colour subtraction alike. Crops 1 and 2 hold only creases.

the same stamp struck twice on this crop, once heavily and once so lightly that only the tops of the figures took ink. In the heavy impression the five figures read 1, 2, 1, 2 and a last figure with a closed counter above and below, so 8; the light impression left only the upper curl of that figure, which alone would read 6 and would give 1926. Both impressions carry the same short double-dash mark before the first figure, so that mark belongs to the stamp device rather than being a figure. Read as 12.1.28 with the separators dropped.

pencil on dark red paper, five figures run together under the paper edge, both panels agree. The 5, the 2 and the last figure, a slanted oval crossed by a stroke and so a 0, are plain. The third figure has a longer top stroke than the second and taken alone could be a 7, but 5.17.20 is no month and 51.7.20 no day, so the only parse is 5.11.20.

notes: no punch date. Crop 2 shows the head of the roll with the printed paper title label pasted on, carrying the catalogue number 2538, the title and the pianist's signature in facsimile, and above it the printed slip about keeping music-rolls in boxes. The roll paper beside the label carries the printed English licence notice of M. Welte & Sons, Inc. Nothing is written by hand. The number 2538 is the printed label's, not a workshop hand. Crops 1 and 3 show only the scanner's QPcard colour target and the leader strap.
